question.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -38 \\ 24\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -38 \\ 24\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & -38 \\ 3 & -3 & 24\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & -38 \\ 3 & -3 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & -19 & -38 \\ 3 & -3 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & -19 & -38 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{12}{19}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & -19 & -38 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0 \\ -19{x}_{2}=-38.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-5(2)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=10.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=10+2=12.$
